claims.text: Combining thermodynamic integration with metadynamics or umbrella sampling can accurately determine melting properties across HEA compositional space.
Machine-learned interatomic potentials optimized for HEAs can accurately represent the interactions needed to predict melting and liquid-phase thermodynamics.
The proposed protocol can determine melting temperature, fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, volume change at melting, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties.
The initial HEA samples are disordered, multicomponent solids before melting.
High-temperature simulations with controlled heating rates at ambient pressure can represent melting conditions comparable to DSC experiments.
Structural disorder and multielement interactions in HEAs create a complex free-energy landscape governing phase transitions.
Enhanced sampling efficiently explores relevant metastable states and transition pathways in the HEA free-energy landscape.
Focusing sampling on relevant metastable states and transitions reduces computational cost.
Capturing multicomponent interactions with machine-learned potentials enables accurate prediction of melting-related thermodynamic variables.
Predicted melting temperatures and fusion properties will have errors near or below 5–10% relative to calibrated experiments or high-fidelity simulation benchmarks.
The protocol will be computationally tractable across a wide range of HEA compositions.
Standard experimental calorimetry and first-principles or molecular-dynamics methods are too slow or insufficiently accurate for the full compositional complexity of HEAs.
The approach is applicable to disordered, multicomponent alloys within mainstream HEA composition space.
Alloys with substantially different bonding or electronic structures may require reparameterization.
Predicted properties may be sensitive to the training dataset and enhanced-sampling parameters.
Deviation greater than approximately 20% from experimental data across tested properties would falsify the proposed approach.
Systematic errors across multiple HEA compositions would falsify the proposed approach.
